messages:
sam: heads-up — controller-manager in eu-west1 is crashlooping and cluster-autoscaler kept spinning up GPU nodes. billing alerted to a ~$8k spike in the last 2h. anyone watching?

maria: omg, on it. seeing a bunch of `CreateNode` events followed by immediate `DeleteNode` for new gpus. logs show controller-manager panics around leader election timeouts. :grimacing:

alex: linking the metrics — etcd commit-latency climbed to >200ms around 02:03 UTC, correlates with a flurry of node annotation writes during our GPU onboarding test. could be kv contention.

kevin: autoscaler logs show repeated scale-outs because pod pending->unschedulable triggers keep firing while controller-manager is flapping (it can't bind pods fast enough). autoscaler then thinks capacity is insufficient and requests more GPU nodes. classic feedback loop.

sam: exact chain we feared. controller-manager crash -> missed pod bindings -> CA scale out -> more nodes -> more etcd writes -> more controller churn.

maria: temporary mitigation: disabled cluster-autoscaler for eu-west1 (patched autoscaler CRD to paused). also cordoned a couple of newly provisioned GPU nodes and set their taints so workloads won't land until we stabilize.

kevin: pushed a quick rollout to controller-manager v1.21.3 (previous stable) from v1.22.0-canary; if the panic is a regression we should stop the churn. deploy-bot: rollout started.

deploy-bot: rollout/controller-manager eu-west1 -> image redwood/controller-manager:v1.21.3 started by kevin.

alex: can we also reduce the rate of GPU node annotation writes? seen a controller that annotates GPU firmware and telemetry every 10s. adding a debounce would help.

maria: opened an issue on infra repo to debounce the gpu-onboard controller (https://git.redwood/infra/issues/1427). short-term we can throttle by adding a per-node annotation queue with a 2m coalesce window.

sam: for immediate stabilization: 1) keep CA paused, 2) rollback controller-manager (kevin did), 3) cordon tainted nodes (maria did), 4) bump etcd io throughput where possible and pause snapshot compactions. any other suggestions?

kevin: I'll bump etcd provisioned IOPS for the next 2 hours in eu-west1 to absorb bursts. also enabling etcd slow-logs at 100ms to capture the heavy ops.

alex: runbook note: if autoscaler is unpaused too soon, we risk another loop. plan to unpause only after controller-manager has been stable for 15m and etcd 95th commit latency <50ms for 10m.

maria: FYI, discovered a kubelet-side flapping bug that retries annotation writes on EADDRINUSE errors; that's amplifying write traffic. filing a patch.

infra-sre: tracking cost impact — finance is aware. estimated incremental cost for the surge ~ $7.9k, we'll prepare a post-incident cost breakdown.

sam: thanks all. next actions: kevin keeps watching controller-manager pods, alex monitors etcd latency and slow-logs, maria tests debounce patch in staging, infra-sre coordinates cost report. I'll leave CA paused and update once we have stable signals. :white_check_mark:

kevin: controller-manager is steady for 6m, no new panics. etcd commit-latency down to ~40ms. I'll wait until 15m then we can consider a controlled unpause.

alex: slow-logs captured a few heavy txn stacks — sending snippets to the owners.

maria: debounce PR created: PR #298 — adds per-node 120s coalescing for annotations. testing now.

sam: closing the immediate loop. will create a short postmortem with timeline and mitigation notes. add any missing notes in this thread before I draft.
